brief:
A photography exhibition documenting Gaza has sparked a solidarity movement in Sarajevo, where residents now gather weekly to read aloud the names of children killed in the territory, Al Jazeera English reported. The exhibition has evolved beyond displays of images into a sustained commemorative practice rooted in the city's own history of mass casualties.

The weekly vigils represent an intensification of Sarajevo's response to Gaza's humanitarian crisis. Participants have moved from viewing photographs to actively naming the dead, drawing a connection between the city's experience during the 1990s conflict and current suffering in Palestinian territories.
dek: From a photography exhibition to a weekly vigil reading out the names of killed children, solidarity grows in Sarajevo.
title: Sarajevo residents mark Gaza dead through photography and weekly vigil
